newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW ELECTRICITY WORTH OVER A$24 BLN - ITA.
newsitem.headline: NSW ELECTRICITY WORTH OVER A$24 BLN - ITA.

text.p: The potential sale of electricity assets by the New South Wales government could raise more than A$24 billion, said John Caldon, managing director of Macquarie Infrastructure Investment Management Ltd (MIIM).
"I think the figure of A$24 billion was mooted, we would suspect it would get more than that rather than less than that," Caldon told reporters.
MIIM is manager of Infrastructure Trust of Australia (ITA).
"I think the figures quoted by the New South Wales government are conservative rather than exaggerated," Caldon said.
"We think the New South Wales assets are extremely attractive -- indeed I am sure they will go very well should be the government be elected to sell them," Caldon said.
The New South Wales (NSW) Labor party government is supporting the proposed sale, which has split the party.
The NSW government was encouraged to sell the electricity assets following the success of the sale of the state of Victoria electricity assets.
